reach.rationale: No experimental/preview APIs at all, but every page depends on TanStack Start, which became formally 1.0-stable 17 days before this review, plus recently-stable srvx 1.0 in the production server — squarely 'recently-stable APIs in central places'.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.functions.ts:1-23 — all server functions centralized in one thin module over pokedex.server.ts
app/server.mjs:1-16 — the only srvx usage is a single self-contained 16-line production server isolating the serving layer
app/src/routes/*.tsx — routes use only long-stable @tanstack/react-router primitives (createFileRoute, notFound, useNavigate)
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; even the framework-specific seams (server functions, custom server) are each isolated behind one module or file, so a future API shift would touch one or two files.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokedex.server.ts:1-60 — createServerFn justified: keeps API fetching, filtering and in-memory caching server-side, unreachable by the client
app/server.mjs:6-16 — srvx fetch-handler server matches TanStack's own node-server/examples pattern (tanstack.com hosting docs, router PR #5915)
app/src/routes/pokemon.$name.tsx:25-33 — stable loader/validateSearch used for the ?game= query requirement instead of any newer experimental routing API
justification.rationale: The framework was mandated by the spec, and each API buys something stable alternatives don't: type-safe server-only data access, and a minimal standards-based prod server. No use is gratuitous.

findings.issue: The whole app rests on @tanstack/react-start, which was only declared 1.0-stable on 2026-10-13; formal API commitment is days old
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change — pin exact minor versions or record the version in a lockfile-driven upgrade policy so future Start releases are adopted deliberately

findings.issue: srvx became 1.0 on 2026-09-02 and is on rapid point releases (1.0.5→1.0.8 within six weeks); a prod server on a two-month-old 1.x carries minor churn risk
findings.suggestion: Acceptable — it's the same library TanStack's own examples use; just watch srvx release notes when bumping

findings.issue: TypeScript 7 (native Go port) went GA 2026-07-08 and drops some 6.x-era APIs; ecosystem tooling support is still catching up
findings.suggestion: Fine as a devDependency for a plain React app; verify editor/CI toolchain compatibility before unrelated upgrades

summary: The app contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs — no unstable_ names, no experimental config flags. Its only newness is that the mandated framework, TanStack Start, reached formal 1.0 stability 17 days ago, with srvx 1.0 and TypeScript 7 also recently stable. All framework seams (server functions, custom srvx server) are cleanly isolated, and every API used is the current stable, documented surface, so experimental risk is minimal.
